newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end down sharply, Canada up.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end down sharply, Canada up.

text.p: Most IMM currencies finished sharply lower after a session dominated by dollar strength.
The dollar/yen recovered overnight from recent weakness, spilling into dollar/mark and dollar/Swiss. The rally drove the U.S. unit to a two-year high against the mark.
March marks stumbled to a fresh contract low at $0.6360 amid concerns over Germany's interest rate outlook before key employment data due Thursday.
Market participants cited expectations for a hefty rise in German joblessness, which could point to a sputtering economy and a possible cut in German short term rates.
Further pressure came from news Russian President Boris Yeltsin had been hospitalized Wednesday with the first signs of pneumonia.
While most currencies sank amid the dollar strength, Canadian dollar rallied on aggressive institutional and technical buying. Traders pegged upside targets in March yen at $0.7500.
"Canada and marks and Swiss selling off was the main activity," a floor maanger at an IMM trading firm said. "The pounds weren't as active as the others," he said.
"We had some pretty good movement on the downside in the pound, but the volume was really thin," the floor manager said.
Traders noted that sterling has been well-bid in recent weeks, but unable to sustain a move above $1.70 resistance. "It's a pretty well-confined market," one futures analyst said.
Players noted how swiftly the bullish dollar tone returned to the market and called recent losses a correction.
"Dollar/yen turned on a dime and retraced its move pretty quickly," one analyst said.
March Swiss francs set a contract low at $0.7362, below double-bottom support from the previous contract low at $0.7386.

At settlement, March yen was down $0.000045 to $0.008721, March marks were down $0.0047 to $0.6377, Swiss francs fell $0.0062 to $0.7376, sterling lost $0.0070 to $1.6848, Canadian dollar rose $0.0031 to $0.7433, Australian dollar fell $0.0097 to $0.7795, and Mexican peso rose $0.000250 to $0.123225.
